title: Universal programming fundamentals
description: Language-agnostic mechanics every problem relies on. Failures here are usually the true root cause even when a higher-level node looks guilty.

nodes.name: Variable initialization & sentinels
nodes.description: Choosing starting values for trackers, accumulators and 'not found' markers that are correct for every valid input.

facets.explain: Can say why an initial value is safe and what input breaks a wrong one (e.g. max = 0 with all-negative input).
facets.implement: Initializes sums/counts to 0, max to arr[0] or INT_MIN, min to arr[0] or INT_MAX, 'not found' to -1.
facets.trace: Resets trackers at the right moment (new streak, new outer iteration, new test case).
facets.adapt: Picks a sentinel that cannot collide with real data, or avoids sentinels by seeding from the first element.

misconceptions.desc: Initialized a max tracker to 0 (or a min tracker to 0); wrong for all-negative / all-positive input.
signals: WA on an all-negative test case

misconceptions.desc: Read an uninitialized local variable (garbage value in C++).
Sentinel (-1, INT_MIN, 0) can also be a real value, so 'not found' and 'found' become indistinguishable.
Did not reset a tracker when its scope ended (streak broke, outer loop advanced).
signals: counter declared outside the outer loop and never zeroed

nodes.name: Zero-based indexing & bounds
nodes.description: Valid indices are [0, n-1]; index expressions like i+1, n-1-i, mid must stay inside them.

facets.implement: Accesses only valid indices and derives index expressions (i+1, n-1-i, (lo+hi)/2) correctly.
facets.trace: Can state the value of every index variable at each step of a dry run.

misconceptions.desc: Accessed arr[i+1], arr[i-1] or arr[n] without guarding the boundary.
signals: arr[i+1] inside for (i = 0; i < n; i++)

misconceptions.desc: Treated the array as 1-indexed (loop 1..n, arr[n] as last element).
Wrong mirrored index (n-i instead of n-1-i).

nodes.name: Loop ranges & off-by-one
nodes.description: Choosing start, end and inclusive/exclusive conditions so each intended element is visited exactly once.

facets.implement: Writes start/end/step so every intended element is processed exactly once.
facets.trace: Can say how many iterations run and which index is processed last.
facets.adapt: Adjusts bounds when the body looks ahead/behind or processes several elements per step.

misconceptions.desc: Used <= n instead of < n (or < n where < n-1 was needed); overruns or skips the last element.
Started at 1 when element 0 must be processed, or at 0 when it must be skipped.
Changed the container size or loop variable inside the loop, skipping elements.
signals: v.erase(...) inside a forward index loop
i++ inside the body of a for loop that also increments i

nodes.name: Comparisons & branching
nodes.description: Strict vs non-strict comparisons, branch ordering, explicit handling of equality.

facets.explain: Can justify which branch equality belongs to.
facets.implement: Uses the right operator (> vs >=) and orders else-if branches so specific cases are not shadowed.

misconceptions.desc: Used > where >= was required or vice versa (ties handled wrongly).
Else-if chain ordered so a more general condition shadows a specific one.
Wrote = instead of == inside a condition.

nodes.name: Nested iteration
nodes.description: Enumerating pairs, triplets and subarrays with dependent loop bounds; the usual brute-force baseline.

facets.recognize: Recognizes nested loops as the brute-force baseline and estimates when they will TLE.
facets.implement: Writes dependent bounds (j = i+1) so each pair/triplet is visited once.
facets.trace: Can count iterations (n², n(n-1)/2) and list which pairs are visited.

misconceptions.desc: Inner loop starts at 0 instead of i+1, so pairs are counted twice or an element pairs with itself.
Inner bound uses the wrong variable (n vs m, i vs j).

nodes.name: Swapping & shifting elements
nodes.description: Exchanging two elements and shifting ranges without overwriting data that is still needed.

facets.implement: Swaps correctly (temp variable or std::swap) and shifts ranges in an order that never loses data.
facets.trace: Tracks array contents after each swap or shift.

misconceptions.desc: Overwrote a value before saving it.
Shifted in an order that overwrites not-yet-moved elements (left shift iterating right-to-left).

nodes.name: Running accumulation
nodes.description: Maintaining running sums, counts and products updated once per element.

facets.implement: Updates the accumulator exactly once per element at the right place in the loop body.
facets.trace: Can state the accumulator's value after each step.

misconceptions.desc: Updated the answer before/after the accumulator in the wrong order (used a stale or future value).
Added an element twice or skipped one because of update placement.

nodes.name: Modulo & wraparound
nodes.description: Reducing k by n and computing wrapped positions; C++ % keeps the dividend's sign.

facets.recognize: Recognizes when positions wrap around (rotation, circular indexing) and when k can exceed n.
facets.implement: Uses k %= n and (i + k) % n correctly, guarding n == 0 and negative operands.

misconceptions.desc: Did not reduce k modulo n; out-of-bounds access or wasted work when k >= n.
Computed k % n when n == 0 (division by zero).
Assumed (i - k) % n is non-negative; in C++ it can be negative.

nodes.name: In-place modification vs auxiliary copy
nodes.description: Knowing what 'in-place / O(1) extra space' means and preserving data that is still needed.

facets.recognize: Notices when the problem forbids extra space or requires modifying the input.
facets.explain: Knows which operations allocate and what counts toward extra space.
facets.trace: Modifies the input without clobbering values that are read later.

misconceptions.desc: Used an auxiliary array when O(1) extra space was required.
Overwrote input values that the algorithm still needed.

nodes.name: Function contract & return values
nodes.description: Returning exactly what the signature and statement require, from every path.

facets.implement: Returns the required thing (index vs value, -1 when absent, count, vector in required order) on every path.

misconceptions.desc: Returned a value instead of an index (or vice versa), or the wrong 'not found' value.
Some path has no return statement (undefined behaviour in C++).
Returned inside the loop on the first iteration (return in both if and else).

nodes.name: 2D indexing (rows & columns)
nodes.description: Addressing mat[r][c] with r < rows and c < cols, including non-square and empty matrices.

facets.implement: Uses separate row/column bounds and never swaps them for non-square input.
facets.trace: Tracks (r, c) as a traversal moves.

misconceptions.desc: Used n for both dimensions or swapped m and n; breaks on non-square matrices.
Read mat[0].size() when the matrix has zero rows.

nodes.name: Recursion basics
nodes.description: Base case, recursive case, combining sub-results, and the call tree.

facets.explain: States the base case, the recursive case and what each call returns.
facets.implement: Writes a terminating recursion that combines sub-results correctly.
facets.trace: Can draw the call tree for a small input.

misconceptions.desc: Missing or wrong base case; infinite recursion / stack overflow.
Made a recursive call but discarded its returned value.
Wrong split point (mid vs mid+1) causing overlap or non-termination.
